units.reading_strategy: Picture the changes in your mind.
reading_chunks: Bella lives in Nome, Alaska. Her father uses a poem to help her imagine her place in the universe.
In her imagination, Bella travels in a spacecraft. Her home looks smaller. Then she sees Earth, the solar system and galaxies.
Bella’s imaginary journey ends. She is back in her bedroom. She wants to imagine visiting those places again.
units.thinking_prompt: As Bella moves farther away, how does Earth look? Draw it near, then far.
units.thinking_frame: At first, I picture ___. Later, I picture ___.
units.grammar_pattern: I think + subject + will + base verb
units.grammar_example: I think we will learn more about space.
units.grammar_note: Use will to say what you think will happen. After will, use the base verb.
units.grammar_frame: I think I will ___ in the future.
grammar_checks: I think people ___ visit more planets.
I will ___ the moon with a telescope.
After will, use the base verb: study.

units.listening_script: Andy and Jenny look at the stars at Grandpa’s farm. They can see the stars clearly because there are fewer bright city lights. Grandpa explains that the Milky Way is our galaxy. Its many stars look like a white belt in the sky.
units.listening_question: Why are the stars easier to see at the farm?
units.listening_answer: There is less light pollution: fewer bright city lights.
units.speaking_frame: In the first picture, I see ___. In the second picture, I see ___.

units.reading_title: Hidden Army: Clay Soldiers of Ancient China
units.reading_strategy: Ask why the author wrote each part.
reading_chunks: The article describes thousands of clay soldiers in ancient China. They were made more than two thousand years ago.
The soldiers do not all look the same. Their faces and uniforms give clues about real soldiers and their ranks.
Archaeologists study the soldiers. Scientists try to protect the remaining paint. In the reading, the emperor’s tomb has not been opened.

units.thinking_frame: The author informs us that ___. I know because ___.
units.grammar_title: Say what you plan or hope to do
units.grammar_pattern: want / plan / hope / decide / try + to + base verb
units.grammar_example: I want to learn about the clay soldiers.
units.grammar_note: An infinitive is to + a base verb. Some verbs are followed by an infinitive.
units.grammar_frame: I want to ___. I plan to ___.
grammar_checks: Want is followed by an infinitive: to be.
They decided to ___ the old objects.

word_study.title: Words with -ist
word_study.note: In these words, -ist names a person who does an activity or job.

units.listening_script: Children describe an ancient town in Bulgaria. People there used salt bricks for trade. Salt helped keep food fresh. Today we often use refrigerators. The ancient town had houses with two floors. Many houses today also have two floors.
units.listening_question: What is one similarity between the ancient town and towns today?
units.listening_answer: Both can have houses with two floors.
units.speaking_frame: I would like to visit ___. I want to see ___ because ___.
units.writing_tip: When you describe a past event, use past-tense verbs together.
units.writing_example: The archaeologist studied the tomb and found old objects.
express_frames: We learn about the past by ___.
units.express_prompt: Explain how old objects help us learn about the past.
quiz: The ancient soldiers in the article were made from ___.
The terracotta soldiers were made from clay.
Who studies old objects to learn about the past?
An archaeologist studies objects from the past.
The soldiers were made of clay.
The material is a fact that informs us.
I want to learn about China.
I want to learning about China.
Keep the past tense consistent: studied and found.
What can uniforms help us learn about?
The reading uses uniforms as clues about soldiers’ ranks.
reading_full: It is 210 BC and the moment before battle. The Chinese emperor's army is ready to charge. The soldiers—thousands of them—are lined up, row after row, as far as the eye can see. However, the army will never attack. The soldiers are not real. They are the size of real soldiers. But they are made of terracotta, a strong kind of clay. They are more than 2,000 years old. Amazingly, no two soldiers are alike. Their faces are different. Some are old; some are young. Some look tired; some look like they can't wait for the battle to start. Their uniforms are different.

The uniforms are exact copies of what real soldiers wore. The archers and foot soldiers were the lowest-ranking soldiers, so they have the plainest uniforms. The generals, of course, wore the most elegant uniforms. Some of their caps had feathers. Sometimes their shoes turned up at the toes. Their armor had small iron rings that look like fish scales. Here you see an image of a clay general. It shows how he looked 2,000 years ago. Every single soldier in the emperor's army was painted with bright colors. So were the terracotta horses. Now most of the soldiers have only tiny traces of paint left. Scientists are trying to create a special varnish to brush over painted figures to hold the paint in place.

Today, craftsmen near the pits where the soldiers were found make copies of the soldiers. This helps archaeologists learn more about how people made the original army. Modern craftsmen have much better kilns than those in ancient times. Kilns are ovens that bake clay until it hardens. Yet no copies ever come out as hard or shiny as the originals. Why? Nobody knows—it is a mystery. An even bigger mystery is what lies inside the emperor's tomb. Nobody knows the answer because the tomb has never been opened. The Chinese government plans to keep it closed for now. Work will not start until archaeologists are sure the tomb can be opened without damaging any of the treasures inside.

As for the emperor's body, according to historical records, it rests in a heavy, bronze coffin. In ancient times, the custom was to dress the dead body of someone important in a suit the Chinese made from hundreds of pieces of thin jade. At that time, jade was more precious than gold. The emperor died when he was 49 years old. Three years after his death, peasants rose up against the empire. One of their leaders started a new royal family. Yet now, millions of people come to the emperor's burial place. They visit the covered pits to see the clay soldiers. The emperor lives on in the memory of all who see his amazing hidden army.

Các tượng lính không giống hệt nhau. Khuôn mặt và đồng phục cho biết thêm về người lính thật và cấp bậc của họ.
Các nhà khảo cổ nghiên cứu những tượng lính. Các nhà khoa học cố bảo vệ lớp màu còn lại. Trong bài đọc, lăng mộ của hoàng đế vẫn chưa được mở.

map.title: Present your will mind map
steps: Use: make a prediction. Form: subject + will + base verb.
Add examples and time expressions: someday, in the future, next year.
Point to each branch and say a whole sentence. Practise, then record your presentation if your teacher asks.
map.help: Chia sơ đồ thành 4 nhánh: cách dùng, cấu trúc, ví dụ, dấu hiệu thời gian. Đây là phần ôn dự đoán; will còn có cách dùng khác.
map.prompt: My mind map: use / form / examples / time expressions

express.title: Five word sentences → a short story
express.vi: Viết câu với từ mới, rồi thử viết truyện ngắn
steps: Choose five picture words. Write one sentence for each.
Try a short imaginary space story using vast, dwelled, disk and speck.
Check that each sentence has a subject and a verb. Use dwelled for an action in the past.
express.help: Viết 5 câu trước. Sau đó nối các ý thành truyện; dwell là dạng nguyên mẫu, dwelled là dạng quá khứ có trong bài đọc.
express.prompt: My five sentences / my space story

map.title: Earth · Both · Venus
map.vi: Venn diagram: so sánh hai hành tinh
steps: Draw two overlapping circles. Label the left Earth, the middle Both, and the right Venus.
Earth: cooler than Venus. Both: almost the same size; a core containing iron and rock. Venus: hotter; thicker clouds.
Say: Both planets ___. Earth ___, but Venus ___. Present your diagram or mind map.
map.help: Giữa hai vòng là điểm giống nhau; hai bên là điểm khác nhau. Dùng thông tin bài đọc, không đoán số liệu.

language.title: First conditional: two clause orders
language.vi: Câu điều kiện loại 1: đổi thứ tự hai vế
steps: If I get a telescope, I will observe the Moon.
I will observe the Moon if I get a telescope. The meaning stays the same.
A simple sentence: I observe the Moon. A complex sentence: If I get a telescope, I will observe the Moon. Find the condition and result.
language.help: Vẽ mind map gồm điều kiện, kết quả, cấu trúc và ví dụ. Vế if dùng hiện tại đơn; vế kết quả dùng will + động từ nguyên mẫu. Khi vế if đứng đầu, dùng dấu phẩy.
language.prompt: My first conditional mind map and two sentence orders

reading.title: What did you learn? At least seven lines
reading.vi: Viết ít nhất 7 dòng theo bài lớp giao
steps: Start with the article topic. Write two similarities between Earth and Venus.
Write two differences. Add something you learned about exploring space.
Finish with your own thought. Write at least seven lines in your notebook; screen wrapping does not count the lines for you.
reading.help: Dùng bài đọc để kiểm tra thông tin. Viết ý bằng câu của em; không chép nguyên đoạn. Ô nhập dưới đây lưu bản nháp.
reading.prompt: I learned that… / Both planets… / Earth…, but Venus… / I think…

express.title: My favourite planet + solar-system model
express.vi: Đoạn văn về hành tinh yêu thích và mô hình hệ Mặt Trời
steps: Name your favourite planet. Give a reason and two facts you can check in the book.
For the class project, label the Sun and eight planets in order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Explain that a classroom model may not show real sizes or distances. Tell someone how gravity keeps planets in orbit.
express.help: Project được ghi trong Excel tuần 28/09–02/10; đặt ở đây vì liên quan hệ Mặt Trời. Không coi kích thước mô hình là tỉ lệ thật.
express.prompt: My favourite planet is… / My reason is… / My model shows…

language.title: Verb patterns: -ing / to / both
language.vi: Bài mở rộng trên lớp: phân loại động từ
steps: -ing: enjoy learning; finish drawing; avoid touching.
to + base verb: want to learn; plan to visit; hope to discover; decide to study.
Both: like learning / like to learn; love drawing / love to draw. Make three branches and add your own examples.
language.help: Đây là bài mở rộng từ nhật ký lớp, không phải toàn bộ grammar của Unit 3. Không phải mọi động từ đều đi với cả hai dạng. Một số động từ như stop hoặc remember đổi nghĩa khi đổi dạng; chưa đưa vào bài phân loại cơ bản này.
language.prompt: My three branches: -ing / to + base verb / both

express.title: Why teamwork is important
express.vi: Viết đoạn: câu chủ đề → ý hỗ trợ → kết luận
steps: Topic sentence: Teamwork is important because people can help one another.
Supporting idea 1: explain a reason, then give an example. Try sharing jobs when making a model.
Supporting idea 2: explain a different reason, then give an example. Try checking one another’s labels.
Concluding sentence: restate your main idea. Check present tense for general ideas and past tense for a past example.
express.help: Bài lớp yêu cầu ít nhất 2 ý hỗ trợ; mỗi ý có giải thích và ví dụ. Câu mẫu là gợi ý tự soạn, không phải đáp án bắt buộc.
express.prompt: Topic sentence / Reason 1 + explanation + example / Reason 2 + explanation + example / Conclusion
